target: AArch64 PCI QEMU, graphical terminal and VirtIO keyboard
evidence: A disposable PCI QEMU guest launched the bundled DebugDemo through XTalk. The original loop emitted a sustained stream of dots. The test drained serial output continuously for at least five seconds after observing the dots, then sent Ctrl-Alt-C through QMP. The guest continued emitting dots and did not respond to a subsequent serial command within 30 seconds. A focused-terminal retest explicitly confirmed sys_focus_task was bootstrap_gui_terminal_task before launch and reproduced the same timeout. An earlier break sent after only three seconds returned control, but did not prove the loop had started and is not counted as a pass.
scope: A separate PCI QEMU positive control, python3 scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-demo-ohgreat, passed Ctrl-Alt-C and terminal recovery while the stock OhGreat loop yielded. This validates chord delivery in that responsive case, not audio output. The busy-loop result demonstrates that the current input-polling path cannot reliably break DebugDemo. It does not establish whether Ctrl-Alt-D debugger entry works, and does not validate live UTM or physical Pi behavior. No scheduler yield was added to MessageScan or to the original demo. An experimental print-boundary input poll was removed after a boot timeout; its cause was not established.

current_recheck.result: fail: after the focused original busy loop produced sustained dots and Ctrl-Alt-C was sent, serial recovery timed out while dots continued
current_recheck.analysis: Current input break is dispatched from cooperative device polling; the general timer interrupt is not an always-on keyboard interrupt. A non-yielding guest loop cannot reliably poll the break chord. Any interrupt delivery must preserve the focused task context and avoid corrupting interrupted kernel or compiler state; MessageScan must remain non-switching.

qemu_interrupt_investigation.command: qemu-system-aarch64 -machine virt,gic-version=3,dumpdtb=build/virt-keyboard-irq.dtb -cpu cortex-a72 -m 1024 -nodefaults -display none; dtc -I dtb -O dts build/virt-keyboard-irq.dtb
qemu_interrupt_investigation.result: The generated QEMU virt device tree assigns SPI numbers 16, 17, ... 47 to VirtIO MMIO slots at 0x0a000000, 0x0a000200, ... 0x0a003e00. GIC interrupt IDs for these SPIs are 48–79. The keyboard driver currently scans for an input-capable slot and polls it; current GIC initialization enables the timer PPI, not these input SPIs.
qemu_interrupt_investigation.next_work: Verify Ctrl-Alt-D, live UTM and Pi behavior. Later checks pass repeated Ctrl-Alt-C with graphical terminal recovery using QEMU VirtIO and USB keyboards, without adding a yield to MessageScan; see terminal-output-investigation-2026-11-09.json. The queue remains finite, and interrupt recognition does not itself stop the app. Physical Pi interrupt behavior remains unverified.
qemu_interrupt_investigation.scope: Opt-in QEMU virt GICv3/MMIO observation acknowledges the keyboard interrupt and scans bounded completed events to count Ctrl-Alt-C; the ordinary polling path alone consumes and reoffers descriptors. It does not deliver a break or switch tasks. USB/xHCI, physical Pi and live UTM are not covered.

irq_observer_test.evidence: QEMU HVF selected MMIO keyboard interrupt ID 79. A five-second non-yielding serial-invoked guest function with RFlagsGet 0x2 saw zero IRQs while a key was sent. A second function temporarily set IF and reported 0x202; it observed two IRQs during its loop. Both keys were delivered to the focused terminal after the loops. After disabling the observer, a further key left its count unchanged and the serial terminal returned 42. The original flags were restored. This does not prove the IRQ mask of the graphical DebugDemo task or that a Ctrl-Alt-C can safely abort it.

debug_entry_recheck.result: fail: focused original DebugDemo continued printing dots after Ctrl-Alt-C; serial recovery timed out
debug_entry_recheck.evidence: A small prelude was sent to the same focused graphical terminal task immediately before loading the unmodified DebugDemo. It reported x86-compatible interrupt-enable bit set at entry. This does not prove the flag remained enabled throughout the demo. The IRQ observer remained disabled for this test.

chord_and_queue_recheck.evidence: With observer enabled, a non-yielding function detected one Ctrl-Alt-C chord before returning when IRQs were enabled. An ordinary key did not count as a chord. The later normal input poll delivered all chord releases; both Ctrl and Alt were clear, a following C was delivered without modifiers, and the terminal returned 42. The QEMU queue size was 32 and the observer reported zero overruns. The observer was then disabled and its interrupt count stayed unchanged. Earlier with eight descriptors, the same experiment left modifiers stuck; a larger bounded queue prevents that sequence but cannot guarantee arbitrary sustained input while polling is stopped.
chord_and_queue_recheck.device_limit_test: make check-virtio-kbd-queue verifies power-of-two selection up to 32 and legacy DMA layout for advertised maxima 0 through 512. Smaller real device queues and legacy transport remain untested in a guest.
